analysis.text: 主干 What does Cat Hobaiter think + 宾语从句 we should do…；for chimp conservation 是目的状语；think 后省略 that。

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: "Sometimes in the rush to conserve the species, I think we forget about the individuals," says Cat Hobaiter, a professor at the University of St. Andrews. "Each population, each community, even each generation of chimps is unique. An event might only have a small impact on the total population of chimps, but it may wipe out an entire community—an entire culture. No matter what we do to restore habitat or support population growth, we may never be able to restore that culture." “在急于保育物种的时候，我们有时忘了个体，”圣安德鲁斯大学教授 Cat Hobaiter 说，“每 个种群、每个社群，甚至每一代黑猩猩都是独特的。一件事情对黑猩猩总数的影响可能很 小，却可能抹掉一整个社群——一整套文化。不管我们怎样恢复栖息地、支持种群增长，那 种文化我们也许永远无法再造。” 54. C) Study the unique characteristics of each generation of chimps. D) Endeavor to restore chimp habitats to expand its total population.

A) Picture yourself at a college graduation day, with a fresh cohort(一群) of students about to set sail for new horizons. What are they thinking while they throw their caps in the air? What is it with this thin sheet of paper that makes it so precious? It's not only the proof of acquired knowledge but plays into the reputation game of where you were trained. Being a graduate from Harvard Law School carries that extra glamour, doesn't it? Yet take a closer look, and the diploma is the perfect ending to the modern tragedy of education.
B) Why? Because universities and curricula are designed along the three unities of French classical tragedy: time, action, and place. Students meet at the university campus (unity of place) for classes (unity of action) during their 20s (unity of time). This classical model has traditionally produced prestigious universities, but it is now challenged by the digitalisation of society—which allows everybody who is connected to the internet to access learning—and by the need to acquire skills in step with a fast-changing world. Universities must realise that learning in your 20s won't be enough. If technological diffusion and implementation develop faster, workers will have to constantly refresh their skills.
C) The university model needs to evolve. It must equip students with the right skills and knowledge to compete in a world 'where value will be derived largely from human interaction and the ability to invent and interpret things that machines cannot', as the English futurist Richard Watson puts it. By teaching foundational knowledge and up-to-date skills, universities will provide students with the future-proof skills of lifelong learning, not just get them 'job-ready'.
D) Some universities already play a critical role in lifelong learning as they want to keep the value of their diplomas. This new role comes with a huge set of challenges, and needs largely to be invented. One way to start this transformation process could be to go beyond the 'five-year diploma model' to adapt curricula to lifelong learning. We call this model the lifelong passport.
E) The Bachelor's degree could be your passport to lifelong learning. For the first few years, students would 'learn to learn' and get endowed with reasoning skills that remain with them for the rest of their lives. For instance, physics allows you to observe and rationalise the world, but also to integrate observations into models and, sometimes, models into theories or laws that can be used to make predictions. Mathematics is the language used to formulate the laws of physics or economy, and to make rigorous computations that turn into predictions. These two disciplines naturally form the foundational pillars of education in technical universities.
F) Recent advances in computational methods and data science push us into rethinking science and engineering. Computers increasingly become principal actors in leveraging data to formulate questions, which requires radically new ways of reasoning. Therefore, a new discipline blending computer science, programming, statistics and machine learning should be added to the traditional foundational topics of mathematics and physics. These three pillars would allow you to keep learning complex technical subjects all your life because numeracy(计算) is the foundation upon which everything else is eventually built.
G) According to this new model, the Master of Science (MSc) would become the first stamp in the lifelong learning journey. The MSc curriculum should prepare students for their professional career by allowing them to focus on acquiring practical skills through projects.
H) Those projects are then interwoven with fast-paced technical modules(模块) learned 'on-the-fly' and 'at will' depending on the nature of the project. If, for instance, your project is developing an integrated circuit, you will have to take a module on advanced concepts in microelectronics. The most critical skills will be developed before the project even starts, in the form of boot camps(短期 强化训练), while the rest can be fostered along with the project, putting them to immediate use and thus providing a rich learning context.
I) In addition to technical capabilities, the very nature of projects develops social and entrepreneurial skills, such as design thinking, initiative taking, team leading, activity reporting or resource planning. Not only will those skills be actually integrated into the curriculum but they will be very important to have in the future because they are difficult to automate.
J) After the MSc diploma is earned, there would be many more stamps of lifelong learning over the years. If universities decide to engage in this learning model, they will have to cope with many organisational challenges that might shake their unity of place and action. First, the number of students would be unpredictable. If all of a university's alumni(往届毕业生) were to become students again, the student body would be much bigger than it is now, and it could become unsustainable for the campus in terms of both size and resources. Second, freshly graduated students would mix with professionally experienced ones. This would change the classroom dynamics, perhaps for the best. Project-based learning with a mixed team reflects the reality of the professional world and could therefore be a better preparation for it.
K) Sound like science fiction? In many countries, part-time studying is not exceptional: on average across OECD countries, part-time students in 2016 represented 20 per cent of enrolment in tertiary education. In many countries, this share is higher and can exceed 40 per cent in Australia, New Zealand and Sweden.
L) If lifelong learning were to become a priority and the new norm, diplomas, just like passports, could be revalidated periodically. A time-determined revalidation would ease administration for everybody. Universities as well as employers and employees would know when they have to retrain. For instance, graduates from the year 2000 would have to come back in 2005.
M) This could fix the main organisational challenges for the university, but not for the learners, due to lack of time, family obligations or funds. Here, online learning might be an option because it allows you to save your 'travel time', but it has its limits. So far, none of the major employers associated with online learning platforms such as Coursera and Udacity has committed to hire or even interview graduates of their new online programmes. N) Even if time were not an issue, who will pay for lifelong learning? That's the eternal debate: should it be the learner's responsibility, that of his employer, or of the state? For example, in Massachusetts, the healthcare professions require continuing education credits, which are carefully evidenced and documented. Yet the same state's lawyers don't require continuing legal education, although most lawyers do participate in it informally. One explanation is that technology is less of a factor in law than it is in healthcare. O) Europe has many scenarios, but the French and Swiss ones are interesting to compare. In France, every individual has a right to lifelong learning organised via a personal learning account that is credited as you work. In Switzerland, lifelong learning is a personal responsibility and not a government one. However, employers and the state encourage continuing education either by funding parts of it or by allowing employees to attend it. P) Universities have a fundamental role to play in this journey, and higher education is in for a change. Just like classical theatre, the old university model produced talent and value for society. P1 Why does social media trigger feelings of loneliness and inadequacy? Because instead of being real life, it is, for the most part, impression management, a way of marketing yourself, carefully choosing and filtering the pictures and words to put your best face forward.

P2 Online "friends" made through social media do not follow the normal psychological progression of an interpersonal relationship. You share neither physical time nor emotional conversations over the Internet. You simply communicate photographs and catchy posts to a diverse group of people whom you have "friended" or "followed" based on an accidental interaction. This is not to say that your social media friends can't be real friends. They absolutely can, but the two are not synonymous. Generally speaking, there are no unfiltered comments or casually taken photos on our social media pages. And, rightfully so, because it wouldn't feel safe to be completely authentic and vulnerable with some of our "friends" whom we don't actually know or with whom trust has yet to be built. Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.

P3 Social media can certainly be an escape from the daily grind, but we must be cautioned against the negative effects, such as addiction, on a person's overall psychological well-being.

P4 As humans, we yearn for social connection. Scrolling( 滚动) through pages of pictures and comments, however, does not provide the same degree of fulfillment as face-to-face interactions do. Also, we tend to idealize others' lives and compare our downfalls to their greatest accomplishments, ending in feelings of loneliness and inadequacy.

P5 Social media can lead people on the unhealthy quest for perfection. Some people begin to attend certain events or travel to different places so that they can snap that "perfect" photo. They begin to seek validation through the number of people who "like" their posts. In order for it to play a psychologically healthy role in your social life, social media should supplement an already healthy social network. Pictures and posts should be byproducts of life's treasured moments and fun times, not the planned and calculated image that one is putting out into cyberspace in an attempt to fill insecurities or unmet needs.

P6 Ultimately, social media has increased our ability to connect with various types of people all over the globe. It has opened doors for businesses and allowed us to stay connected to people whom we may not otherwise get to follow. However, social media should feel like a fun experience, not one that contributes to negative thoughts and feelings. If the latter is the case, increasing face-to-face time with trusted friends, and minimizing time scrolling online, will prove to be a reminder that your social network is much more rewarding than any "like," "follow" or "share" can be. 46. What does the author imply social media may do to our life? A) It may facilitate our interpersonal relationships. B) It may filter our negative impressions of others. C) It may make us feel isolated and incompetent. D) It may render us vulnerable and inauthentic.

P1 Imagine that an alien species landed on Earth and, through their mere presence, those aliens caused our art to vanish, our music to homogenize, and our technological know-how to disappear. That is effectively what humans have been doing to our closest relatives—chimps(大猩猩).

P2 Back in 1999, a team of scientists led by Andrew Whiten showed that chimps from different parts of Africa behave very differently from one another. Some groups would get each other's attention by rapping branches with their knuckles(指关节), while others did it by loudly ripping leaves with their teeth. The team identified 39 of these traditions that are practiced by some communities but not others— a pattern that, at the time, hadn't been seen in any animal except humans. It was evidence, the team said, that chimps have their own cultures. Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.

P3 It took a long time to convince skeptics that such cultures exist, but now we have plenty of examples of animals learning local traditions from one another.

P4 But just when many scientists have come to accept the existence of animal cultures, many of those cultures might vanish. Ammie Kalan and her colleagues have shown, through years of intensive fieldwork, that the very presence of humans has eroded the diversity of chimp behavior. Where we flourish, their cultures wither. It is a bitterly ironic thing to learn on the 20th anniversary of Whiten's classic study.

P5 "It's amazing to think that just 60 years ago, we knew next to nothing of the behavior of our sister species in the wild," Whiten says. "But now, just as we are truly getting to know our primate(灵长 类) cousins, the actions of humans are closing the window on all we have discovered."

P6 "Sometimes in the rush to conserve the species, I think we forget about the individuals," says Cat Hobaiter, a professor at the University of St. Andrews. "Each population, each community, even each generation of chimps is unique. An event might only have a small impact on the total population of chimps, but it may wipe out an entire community—an entire culture. No matter what we do to restore habitat or support population growth, we may never be able to restore that culture."

P7 No one knows whether the destruction of chimp culture is getting worse. Few places have tracked chimp behavior over long periods, and those that have are also more likely to have protected their animals from human influence.

P8 Obviously, conservationists need to think about saving species in a completely new way—by preserving animal traditions as well as bodies and genes. "Instead of focusing only on the conservation of genetically based entities like species, we now need to also consider culturally based entities," says Andrew Whiten.

writing.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay on why students should be encouraged to develop the ability to meet challenges. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
writing.model: In an era of rapid change, students inevitably encounter difficulties in their studies, career hunting and daily life. It is therefore of great importance that they be encouraged to develop the ability to meet challenges. There are several convincing reasons why this ability deserves cultivation. To begin with, facing challenges pushes students to unlock their hidden potential. A first-year student who dares to tackle a tough research project, for instance, often discovers strengths he never knew he possessed. More importantly, meeting challenges sharpens one's resilience and problem-solving skills. Every setback in a competition or an internship teaches valuable lessons that no textbook can offer. As a result, such students grow into independent thinkers who refuse to give up easily. In conclusion, since the ability to meet challenges prepares young people for fierce competition and lifelong growth, schools and families should spare no effort to foster it. Only by embracing challenges rather than avoiding them can students truly become masters of their own future.

translation.reference: Located 46 kilometers south of Tian'anmen Square, Beijing Daxing International Airport was put into use on September 30, 2019. sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 机场作主语，并列两个谓语「位于」与「投入使用」（主语策略：原句主语） 中文主语明确就是 北京大兴国际机场，主干即「机场 + 位于 + 处」。后半句 于2019年9月30日投 入使用 的主语仍是机场，被动含义（机场被投入使用），主干立为 Beijing Daxing International Airport is located… and was put into use…。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「以南46公里处」作地点状语，两个动作并列 天安门广场以南46公里处 不是主干，降级为介词短语作地点状语：46 kilometers south of Tian'anmen Square。两个动作「位于」「投入使用」时间属性不同（一个是现状、一个是过去事 件），不强行 and 平铺，宜拆为两套：is located… 与 was put into use on September 30, 2019，用关系或分句衔接更清楚。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 「位于」是长期事实，回指全篇基调用一般现在时 is located；「投入使用」是2019年已完成的一 次性动作，偏离基调改用一般过去时 was put into use。 语态 「投入使用」是机场「被」投入使用，中文无被动标记但语义被动，译英须用被动 was put into use，这是汉语主动、英语被动的典型。 日期格式 「2019年9月30日」英文写 September 30, 2019 或 on 30 September 2019，介词用 on（具体 某一天），不要漏掉 on。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Located 46 kilometers south of Tian'anmen Square, Beijing Daxing International Airport was put into use on September 30, 2019. 2. 该巨型工程于2014年开工建设，高峰时工地上有4万多工人。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 前半「工程」作主语被动建设，后半用 There be 表存在（主语策略：原句主语） 前半句主语是 该巨型工程（the massive project），「开工建设」是被建设，主干 The massive project began construction / construction began。后半 高峰时工地上有4万多工人 是典型「某 处有某物」，主干用 There be：there were more than 40,000 workers。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「于2014年」「高峰时」作时间状语，两分句拆开 于2014年 是时间状语 in 2014；高峰时 译 at the peak / at its peak 作状语。前后两分句话题不 同（一是开工、一是用工规模），不宜 and 一路平铺，可拆成两句，或前句作主句、后句用 when/with 衔接。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 「2014年开工建设」是过去已完成事件，偏离现在时基调，用一般过去时 began；「高峰时有工 人」描述的是过去那段时间的状态，同样用过去时 there were。 数词与单复数 「4万多」译 more than 40,000 / over 40,000，workers 用复数；注意英文万位无单独词，4万 即 40,000。 语态 「工程开工建设」是工程被着手建设，可用 construction of the project began（让 construction 作主语）规避主动被动纠结，也可 the project broke ground。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Construction of this massive project began in 2014, and at the peak there were more than 40,000 workers on the construction site. 3. 航站楼设计紧凑，可以允许最大数量的飞机直接停靠在最靠近航站楼中心的位置，这给乘客 提供了极大的方便。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 「航站楼」作主语，核心动词「允许」立主干，末句「这」复指（主语策略：原句主语） 主语是 航站楼（the terminal）。三个分句中「允许…停靠」是核心动作，主干 The compact design of the terminal allows… to dock，把 航站楼设计紧凑 处理成主语 The compact design。末句 这给乘客提供了极大的方便 的「这」复指前面整件事，作末尾的承接。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「设计紧凑」提为主语，「最靠近中心的位置」作后置定语，结果句用 which 降级 航站楼设计紧凑 名词化为主语 The compact design of the terminal。最靠近航站楼中心的位置 用介词短语/定语 the positions closest to the center of the terminal 后置修饰 dock。末句 这 给乘客提供了极大的方便 用非限定定语从句 which provides great convenience for passengers 挂在主句后，避免另起松散的「This provides…」。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 全句描述航站楼的设计特性与功能，是长期现状，回指基调用一般现在时 allows / provides。 主谓一致 主语是 The compact design（单数核心名词），谓语用第三人称单数 allows；which 从句指代整 件事，谓语 provides 亦用单数。别被中间复数名词 aircraft 带偏。 比较级最高级 「最大数量的飞机」the maximum number of aircraft（aircraft 单复数同形）；「最靠近中心」 用 closest to the center，最高级前加 the。 搭配 「给乘客提供方便」用 provide convenience for passengers，介词搭配 provide sth. for sb.； 「停靠」用 dock / park。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The compact design of the terminal allows the maximum number of aircraft to dock directly at the positions closest to its center, which provides great convenience for passengers. 4. 航站楼共有82个登机口，但乘客通过安检后，只需不到8分钟就能抵达任何一个登机口。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 前半「航站楼有82个登机口」、后半「乘客」作主语，but 转折（主语策略：原句主语） 前半 航站楼共有82个登机口 主语是 terminal，主干 The terminal has 82 gates（或 There are 82 gates）。后半 乘客通过安检后…就能抵达 主语换成 passengers，主干 passengers can reach any gate。两半由 但 连接，是隐含的转折/对比（口子虽多，但到达却很快）。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「通过安检后」作时间状语，「不到8分钟」作时间状语，but 显转折 乘客通过安检后 降级为时间状语从句 after passing through security check 或介词短语 after security。只需不到8分钟 作时间状语 in less than 8 minutes。前后用 but / yet 连接，把「登机 口多」与「到达却快」的对比挑明。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 全句是机场的常态能力，回指基调用一般现在时 has / can reach；状语从句 after passengers pass / have passed security 用现在时即可。 单复数 「82个登机口」82 gates 复数；「任何一个登机口」any gate 用单数（any + 单数可数名词）。 数量表达 「不到8分钟」译 in less than 8 minutes / within 8 minutes，less than 修饰数量；介词 in 表 「在……时间内完成」。 连接词 「但」是逻辑转折，用 but / yet 连接两个分句，显出「口虽多、到达却快」的对比，不要漏掉这 个转折词。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The terminal has 82 boarding gates in total, but after passing through security check, passengers can reach any gate in less than 8 minutes. 5. 机场的设计可确保每小时300架次起降。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 「机场的设计」作主语，「确保」作谓语（主语策略：原句主语） 主语是 机场的设计（the airport's design），核心动词「确保」作谓语，主干 The design of the airport ensures…，宾语是 每小时300架次起降 这一名词化结果（300 takeoffs and landings per hour）。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 本句结构简单，「每小时300架次起降」名词化作宾语 句子短、主干清晰，无需大幅降级。仅把 每小时300架次起降 处理为名词短语 300 takeoffs and landings per hour 作 ensures 的宾语，per hour 作频率状语。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 描述设计的长期能力，回指基调用一般现在时 ensures。 主谓一致 主语 The design 是单数，谓语第三人称单数 ensures。 单复数 「300架次起降」takeoffs and landings 都用复数（300架次显然不止一次）。 搭配 频率「每小时」用 per hour / an hour；「确保」ensure 后直接接名词宾语，无需 ensure of。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The design of the airport ensures 300 takeoffs and landings per hour. 6. 机场年客运量2040年将达到1亿人次，有望成为世界上最繁忙的机场。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 前半「年客运量」作主语将达到，后半「机场」有望成为（主语策略：原句主语） 前半 机场年客运量2040年将达到1亿人次 主语是 the airport's annual passenger volume，谓语 「将达到」will reach；后半 有望成为世界上最繁忙的机场 主语回到机场 it，主干 it is expected to become the busiest airport。两半可拆，也可让后半作前半的结果。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 「2040年」作时间状语，后半「有望成为」用 and 接被动预测 2040年 作时间状语 by 2040（用 by 表「到……时」）。后半 有望成为世界上最繁忙的机场 主语 换成机场，用 and is expected to become… 衔接，或独立成句 It is expected to become…；世 界上最繁忙的机场 用最高级 the busiest airport in the world。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 「2040年将达到」是对未来的预测，偏离现在时基调用一般将来时 will reach；「有望成为」用 is expected to become。 语态 「有望」语义被动（被各方预期），用 be expected to 被动结构，主语是被预期的机场。 数字与单位 「1亿人次」译 100 million (passenger trips)；亿在英文是 hundred million，1亿即 100 million，million 在数词后不加 s。 最高级 「世界上最繁忙的」the busiest airport in the world，最高级 busiest 前加 the，范围用 in the world。
